title: Timeless records, reissues and fairness to creative artists
summary: She says the older music is timeless, welcomes reissues, and complains record companies shelve records that will not sell a million.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I'm not saying it wasn't -- it wasn't good, maybe, but it just didn't get to me, you know, it didn't get to me. And like these particular things. I can sit today and listen to some of those things and really, it turns me on right now, you know?

They are absolutely timeless. They are absolutely timeless and I think that in time to come, I've often wondered just what's going to happen with this particular phase of music, you know, in time to come. If it dies out. We can't let it die out, we just can't.
Oh, no, absolutely not. Well, at least it is encouraging that there are many, many reissues. A lot of companies are reissuing things that were on 78 and the early LP material.
Repackaging them and I'm sure they wouldn't be doing it if there wasn't a market for it.

Well, there is a market. There's a market for anything that has ever happened one time, if it's been big and good. Just like Elvis Presley, for instance. Of course we're talking about years ahead of what we're talking about now, but I'll use him, and you know, there is a market.

Anybody who has ever made any -- got any recognition, earned any recognition, I think there's always a place for it, I really do. Because it means that there's something unique there, there's something different, and I think there's always a place for it. And I don't think that it's fair for record companies to do as they have done in the past, you know. Well, they can't make a million dollars off a record, so forget it, the record's pushed aside or put on the shelf someplace. And this is most unfair to the artists. It's most unfair to people who have created music, because when you are in this capacity you're creative, you know.
And you cannot replace a creative talent. You just cannot. And we've had some mighty fine creative people in our business.
In the past and of course now, I'm not talking about the now thing. We know what's happening now. But I'm talking about what's happened, you know, before.
